decision_reason: The calibrated host workload shows lower USER_NOTIF workload time, but it does not measure an application-wide slowdown or supersede Tier E's asynchronous attribution and delivery contract. The two dictionary emission modes are statistically indistinguishable on this workload.

provenance.workload_contract: Each verified shared-openat operation performs 1,500,000 deterministic CPU rounds after the syscall.

interpretation.dictionary_mode_selection: No measured winner: unique-edge minus full-stream crosses zero.
interpretation.cross_backend_result: Both USER_NOTIF variants are faster than both dictionary modes in this calibrated host workload; all four direct intervals exclude zero.
interpretation.user_notif_stack_result: The stack-enabled minus no-stack USER_NOTIF interval crosses zero, so this workload cannot isolate a reliable added stack-retrieval cost.
interpretation.inline_status: Excluded from this long-run matrix because its terminal inline snapshot exceeds the independently enforced 64 MiB retained-state cap; that is an explicit incomplete outcome, not a performance observation.
interpretation.scope_limit: These are workload-batch effects on one host, kernel, JDK, image, and pinned CPU pair. They are not whole-application slowdown estimates.
